header.title: The proofs' inventory: every theorem and identity of the law and the supplement with its machine check
header.rule: A check replaces a hand with a machine and changes no claim of the paper or the law; the paper's marks do not move by it. Every row quotes a statement with its place, names its ground and its kind, and names the check that holds it, exactly or to its stated order, or says why none does. A row whose statement as printed fails its check is a finding, reported to the Boss and never smoothed in the files; its check reproduces the discrepancy and returns False.
header.order: the owner's 2026-10-04, 07:50 UTC, through the Boss; the advisor's design lines, #1793 comment 5977935062; the far-regime witnesses the owner's 08:20 UTC
header.heads: every statement is quoted at the head named; where the text moved between the first read and the head (the audit's corrections 5f5df82b and 9775922e, the convention rows d7e97674, fill 17's pushes seven and eight on main), the row's note names both
header.ids: A the audit's ten items, L the law's and the supplement's lines, R the far-regime rows and the heads' new claims, F the rows raised as findings at the first read (the verdict is against the head), N the rows with no check

kinds.A: an exact identity, polynomial or trigonometric in the law's integers, checked exactly in Python's integers, Fractions and Gaussian rationals at random rational witnesses with the symmetric cases forced (a trigonometric identity at the Pythagorean rational points of the circle is a polynomial identity), or a derivative identity by the centred difference's order 2
kinds.B: a series expansion with its order, checked by the residual against the exact function at two step sizes, the ratio 2^order the test of the order, with the far end of the claim's domain computed beside the claim
kinds.C: a hand proof with a numerical witness only: the witness recomputed where a script exists, counted by the ratchet as unchecked
kinds.D: a statement of the engine's structure that only a test of the engine shows: no check here, the engine's tests named

verdicts.holds: the check returns True: the statement holds exactly or to its stated order
verdicts.witness only: a hand proof whose numerical witness the check recomputes; counted as unchecked
verdicts.finding: the statement as printed fails; the check reproduces the discrepancy and returns False
verdicts.none: no check applies; the row says why

rows.name: Theorem 4's Yukawa exponent
rows.place: main.tex 7.2, Theorem 4; S.13; the writer's (1), the advisor's (1)
rows.statement: A Yukawa kernel's log-derivative at one separation is 1 + kappa R; a body's integrated well energy has the running exponent s(R) = 1 + kappa R <u^2> / <u> in the body's own weights, 1.0176, 2.130, 2.971, 2.9997 at kappa R = 0.01, 1, 10, 100, from 1 at kappa R << 1 to the contact kernel's 3 at kappa R >> 1 through 2 at 0.821; the virial and the second variation stand with s the integrated exponent, and R^2 F'' carries R s'(R) W.
rows.ground: the Gaussian body's well moments in closed form through erfc (I = 2 - 2 sqrt pi z erfcx z, J = -4 z + (2 + 4 z^2) sqrt pi erfcx z), the asymptotes by the residual's order
rows.note: The paper's sentence at 2836519e, 's(R) = 1 + kappa R ... holds in the two asymptotic regimes', held at kappa R << 1 and failed at kappa R >> 1 (the audit's item 1); main 7.2 and S.13 since 9775922e print the integrated exponent, 2.130 at kappa R = 1, 2.971 at 10 and the crossing of 2 at 0.82, recomputed.
rows.far_regime_witness: kappa R = 100: the integrated exponent 2.9997 against the printed large end 3 (3 - 3 / z^2 + O(z^-4)) and against 1 + kappa R = 101 of the sentence at 2836519e; the small end 1 + sqrt pi kappa R + O(z^2) to its order

rows.name: The time-Link recurrence's Wronskian
rows.place: main.tex 5.5, S.9, S.33 and ALGEBRA.md row 9 of The conventions and the units, the two-angle form at every place since d7e97674; the writer's (2), the advisor's (2)
rows.statement: The law's step e^(i theta_t) z_next + e^(-i theta_(t-1)) z_before = M z_now / w conserves W_i = Im(conj(z_now) e^(-i theta_(t-1)) z_before) under the per-Node continuity identity for any paces, Link phases and time angles, and the weighted total SUM W_i / p_i^2 exactly; the one-theta form of 5.5 conserves W at a static angle only, |z_2| = 1.93 against the law's 1.00 at the audit's one-Node witness.
rows.ground: exact Gaussian rationals on four periodic boards with Link factors; the audit's witness in floats
rows.note: The slip was the paper's 5.5 sentence at 2836519e (one theta on both levels); since d7e97674 main 5.5, S.9 and S.33 print the two-angle step with the Wronskian booked from the turned levels and conserved exactly for any level in time, as the law's row 9 and the engine's rotation act have it; the one-theta witness is kept as the contrast.

rows.name: S.42's monopole
rows.place: S.42, inputs and (c); the writer's (3), the advisor's (3)
rows.statement: At static non-uniform paces the conserved monopole is the weighted sum SUM_i W_i / p_i^2 (S.33 (a), S.9's D M symmetric), the plain sum its uniform-pace case; at the audit's two-Node witness, paces squared (1, 2) and couplings (a, 2 a), the weighted sum stands exactly while the plain sum moves.
rows.ground: exact Gaussian rationals at random levels and self coefficients
rows.note: S.42's input at 2836519e, the plain sum 'exactly conserved for a static self-level', was the audit's finding; since 9775922e S.42 prints the weighted sum with 'the plain sum its uniform-pace case', row F05's check.

rows.name: S.39 (b)'s band is real for every pair
rows.statement: kappa is the static kernel's fall per Link, cosh kappa = 3 den / num - 2; with S = 0 at the vacuum's paces 2 cos omega = (2 num / 3 den) SUM_a cos k_a runs from 2 num / den to -2 num / den, within [-2, 2] for every pair with num <= den, so no quantum stands 'above the band's top' and the clause does not follow from kappa > 1; [1, 2] has cosh kappa = 4 and the band from 60 to 120 degrees.
rows.ground: exact rationals at the zone's corners and random cosines for every pair to den = 39
rows.note: S.39 (b)'s clause at 2836519e, 'a range below one Link, whose quanta would be above the band's top', reads since 5f5df82b 'where the kernel's lattice sum departs from its continuum integral'; the band's reality for every pair stands as the check.

rows.name: S.43 (e)'s Stark sentence
rows.statement: A uniform static Link phase is a gauge on an open domain (the step with the phases is conjugate to the plain one by the diagonal e^(i theta x), the modes unchanged) and a holonomy on the periodic board (the conjugation fails at the wrap unless N theta is a multiple of 2 pi; it shifts the allowed k and mixes no mode of a body); Stark's shift needs a holder level with a gradient across the body at omega_L = 0.
rows.ground: exact Gaussian rationals on an open and a periodic chain of six
rows.note: S.43 (e) since 9775922e: 'a static holder level with a gradient across the body (omega_L = 0, grad b_L not 0) mixes the modes without a transition, Stark's shift; a uniform static phase is a gauge', the check's content.

rows.name: S.17's beat
rows.place: S.17; main.tex 7.5; the writer's (6), the advisor's (6)
rows.statement: The finite window's mean of the cross current of two standing records is the sum-frequency term's, bounded by 2 / ((omega_1 + omega_2) n T_b) for n beats of length T_b: 0.0083 over one beat at A = B = num = 1, omega_1 = 0.4, omega_2 = 0.4 + 2 pi / 20, and 1.1 x 10^-4 over 100 beats (the bounds 0.09 and 0.0009), falling as 1 / n and never 0 at a finite window.
rows.ground: a hand bound on the oscillating sum; the means and the bounds recomputed, the inequality at random phases
rows.note: S.17 at 2836519e printed 'its mean over the beat is 0'; since 9775922e 'its mean over n beats is 0 to the order of the fast term over the window, 1 / ((omega_1 + omega_2) n T_b) with T_b the beat's length', the bound the witness recomputes.

rows.name: S.24's orientation
rows.place: S.24 and main.tex 10.2; the writer's (7), the advisor's (7)
rows.statement: The directional k^4 coefficient C(n) = (3 SUM_a n_a^4 - 1) / 24 is 1 / 12 on an axis, 1 / 48 on a face diagonal and 0 on the body diagonal, continuous toward it (C / C_axis = 4.4 x 10^-11 at n proportional to (1.00001, 1, 1), the Link bound weakening by 1.5 x 10^5 there); the mean over directions, <SUM n_a^4> = 3 / 5, gives C_mean / C_axis = 2 / 5; the bound weakens tenfold only within about 4 degrees of a body diagonal, one percent of the sky, and a hundredfold within 0.4 degrees.
rows.ground: C(n) as the band's own fourth order (proofs_band), the caps by bisection over the azimuths
rows.note: S.24 since 9775922e prints 'The orientation', C(n), the mean's 2 / 5 and the caps of 4 and 0.4 degrees, and main 10.2 the sentence on the bounds' comparison; recomputed.
rows.far_regime_witness: the eight body diagonals, where the bound is void: the caps of 4.1 and 0.41 degrees, 1.0 and 0.01 percent of the sky

rows.name: S.57's wall
rows.statement: One quantum's inflow is Phi_A + Phi_B <= W_c sin Omega, the born unit, and s_X = eta Phi_X / (W_c sin Omega), so complete equal absorption gives s = eta / 2 and P(neither) = 1 - eta, where the rule at 2836519e, s_X = eta Phi_X / W_c, would leave 1 - eta sin Omega (S.57 since 9775922e prints the born unit W_c sin Omega in the wall and in the transfer); alpha = 0 for one quantum under the one draw, and for two quanta 1 / 2 by the mean counts and 2 / (2 - s)^2 per trial, 8 / 9 at s = 1 / 2.
rows.ground: exact rationals

rows.name: 10.2's 'hence'
rows.statement: Reversibility to the bit with no loops does not by itself give no running of alpha and no Lamb shift; the ground is S.37's 'no pair is created and no coupling runs' from the count's conservation between clicks, the writer's word 'and, with no pair created between clicks (S.37),'.
rows.ground: a sentence's ground; no quantity to compute
rows.note: No machine check applies to a sentence's logical ground; main 10.2 since 9775922e carries the premise, 'with no pair created between clicks (S.37)'.

rows.name: S.26 (d')'s balance at every step
rows.statement: The gain side is exact: the discrete form H_t = (1 / 2) |l_(t+1) - l_t|^2 - (1 / 2) l_(t+1) . L l_t of the holder's line with L symmetric changes per step by exactly (1 / 2) s_t . (l_(t+1) - l_(t-1)); the loss side is the finite sine difference T [sin omega - sin(omega - Delta theta)] = 2 T cos(omega - Delta theta / 2) sin(Delta theta / 2); their ratio is kappa (1 + (Delta theta / 2) tan omega_s + O(Delta theta^2)), so the balance closes to first order in the turn with the remainder (Delta theta / 2) tan omega_s, below 10^-18 at nature's turn and not 0.
rows.ground: the gain identity exact with a random symmetric L, the sine difference exact at rational half-angles, the remainder by the residual's order
rows.far_regime_witness: the largest turn the law allows (the tangent half-angle at most 1, Delta theta = pi / 2): the exact ratio at [2, 3] is 1.348 against the first order's 1.878, so 'at every step and for every motion' is first order in the turn, as S.26 (d') since 9775922e says, 'to first order in the turn at every step and for every motion', the remainder (Delta theta / 2) tan omega_s printed

rows.name: The line's band identity
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The line; row 3 of The conventions and the units; S.1
rows.statement: A plane wave A cos(k . x - omega t) in the line without its remainder leaves the residual a_now [2 w cos omega - S - 2 SUM_a R_a cos k_a], so it solves the line iff 2 w cos omega = S + 2 SUM_a R_a cos k_a.

rows.name: The band at a pace, the Lorentz form
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The line (The clock once and the Link twice), The band at a pace; the paper's Eq. (4); S.1
rows.statement: cos omega = 1 - (1 - num / den) (p_0 / Gamma)^2 - (num / (3 den)) SUM_a (p_a / Gamma)^2 (1 - cos k_a) equals (S + 2 SUM_a R_a cos k_a) / (2 w) with the law's coefficients.

rows.name: The vacuum's band and light's dispersion
rows.place: row 3 of The conventions and the units; S.1; main.tex 3.3
rows.statement: At the vacuum's paces S = 12 num Gamma^2 - 6 R = 0 and cos omega = (num / (3 den)) SUM_a cos k_a, the gap cos omega_0 = num / den; light has cos omega = (2 + cos k) / 3 along an axis; rule3.plane_wave_dispersion is the same number.

rows.name: The clocks shift alike
rows.statement: At k = 0 every massive band's rest rotation obeys 1 - cos omega_b = (p_0 / Gamma)^2 (1 - cos omega_0), one factor for every family.
rows.ground: exact rationals from the band at a pace

rows.name: The guard's edge
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The guard; S.3; S.61 row 4; main.tex 3.4
rows.statement: The mode at wave number pi on every axis has the factor (S - 2 SUM_a R_a) / w = 2 - 2 (1 - num / den) (p_0 / Gamma)^2 - 4 (num / den) (p_a / Gamma)^2, -2 num / den in the vacuum, at or above -2 exactly when p^2 (den + |num|) <= 2 den Gamma^2 (the k = 0 mode for a negative numerator), the edge P^2 = 2 den Gamma^2 div (den + |num|), Gamma^2 for light.
rows.ground: exact rationals over every pace to 2 Gamma; rule3.guard_edge_squared

rows.name: The total mirror of light
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The band at a pace; the derivation script paces.py
rows.statement: Light's record is evanescent where cosh kappa = (Gamma / p_a)^2 (1 - cos k) - 1 > 1, that is p_a < Gamma sin(k / 2), e^(-2 U) below sin(k / 2) under the composed paces: c above 1,733 at lambda = 4 Links and 2,464 at 4.78 at Gamma = 10^4.

rows.name: The three exact bands
rows.statement: The one-Node line at rest is exact in integers only where 2 cos omega_0 is an integer, so the rule carries exactly three exact rotations, 2 cos omega_0 = 1, 0 and -1, the periods 6, 4 and 3, the pairs [1, 2], [0, 1] and [-1, 2].
rows.ground: the integer matrix [[m, -1], [1, 0]] and its orders

rows.name: The band's top on the diagonal and the axis
rows.statement: Along the body diagonal light's band is omega = q exactly, no dispersion; along an axis the top at k = pi has cos omega = 1 / 3, omega = 1.231, sin omega = 0.943.
rows.ground: exact at rational cosines; the axis's numbers in floats

rows.name: The largest group speed
rows.statement: On the full band v_g is largest at k = (pi / 2, pi / 2, pi / 2), (num / den) / sqrt 3 = c cos omega_0, 0.3849 at [2, 3].
rows.ground: the value exact; the maximum over a grid of the zone a witness

rows.name: The content's index for every family
rows.statement: A stationary boundary conserving omega gives 1 - cos k_in = [1 - cos k + 3 (den - num) (1 - N^2) / num] / N^4 exactly; for light sin(k_in / 2) = sin(k / 2) / s with s = N^2; the phase index (2 / k) arcsin(sin(k / 2) / s) = 1 / s + k^2 (1 / s^3 - 1 / s) / 24 + O(k^4), to first order in U 1 + [4 tan(k / 2) / k] U, 1.380 at k = pi / 2 and s = 0.8.
rows.ground: the exact lines in Fractions; the expansions by the residual's orders 4 and 2
rows.far_regime_witness: k = pi / 2 at s = 0.8: the exact ratio 1.380 against the ray limit's 1 / s = 1.25, the chromatic dispersion the ray limit lacks

rows.name: The slow matter's index limit
rows.statement: The 1 / k^2 term of the slow index, 12 (den - num) U / (num m*^2 v^2) = [4 (1 - cos omega_0) / (3 cos omega_0 tan^2 omega_0)] U / v^2, tends to (2 / 3) U / v^2 = 2 Phi / v^2 as omega_0 -> 0, nature's index for a slow body.
rows.ground: the identity in floats to 10^-9, the limit by the residual's order 2
rows.far_regime_witness: the coefficient 0.533 at [2, 3] against the small-gap 2 / 3

rows.name: The reach of a holder with a gap
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The well; S.11; S.39's check
rows.statement: cosh kappa = 3 den / num - 2 from 6 den = num (2 cosh kappa + 4); kappa^2 = 6 den / num - 6 to the second order in the gap; [1, 2] has cosh kappa = 4, e^(-kappa) = 0.127; R = sqrt(num / (6 (den - num))) = 20.00 at [2400, 2401]; inside a thick body the rest is 3 den sigma / (num kappa^2); Yukawa's identity c / omega_g = R sqrt(den / num) to the gap's first order.
rows.ground: exact rationals; the two expansions by the residual's orders 2 and 1

rows.name: The group velocity
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The band at a pace; S.1; rule3.group_velocity
rows.statement: d omega / dk = (R_a / w) sin k / sin omega = (num / (3 den)) (p_a / Gamma)^2 sin k / sin omega along an axis, the vacuum's (num / (3 den)) sin k / sin omega.
rows.ground: the centred difference quotient of the band's omega(k), order 2 at halving

rows.name: Light's speed and dispersion
rows.place: S.1; ALGEBRA.md, The lattice constants; main.tex 10.2
rows.statement: For [1, 1] along an axis cos omega = 1 - k^2 / 6 + k^4 / 72 + O(k^6), omega = (k / sqrt 3) (1 - k^2 / 36 + O(k^4)) and d omega / dk = (1 / sqrt 3) (1 - k^2 / 12 + O(k^4)): the speed 1 / sqrt 3 at long wavelength and the group speed falling as 1 - 0.083 k^2; S.1's check -0.0833, -0.0834, -0.0835 at k = 0.05, 0.1, 0.2.
rows.ground: the residuals' orders 6, 5 and 4; the numbers recomputed

rows.name: The fourth order of light's band
rows.place: S.24; ALGEBRA.md, The law's own formulas B (11)
rows.statement: The k^4 coefficient of omega^2 along n is 1 / 108 - SUM_a n_a^4 / 36: -1 / 54 on an axis, 0 on the body diagonal, -1 / 135 on the directional mean (<n_a^4> = 1 / 5); the anisotropies, an axis against the face diagonal k^2 / 48 in phase and k^2 / 16 in group, against the body diagonal k^2 / 36 and k^2 / 12.
rows.ground: each coefficient by the residual's order 6 along its direction, the mean exact

rows.name: Rule3's coefficients are the read's own without tension
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The paces (The clock is the Node's, the tension is the Link's); rule3.coefficients
rows.statement: At q_ij = Gamma the Link's read coefficient 2 num p_i^2 q_ij^2 / Gamma^2 is rule3's R_a = 2 num p_a^2 at p_a = p_i = p_0^2 / Gamma and the self coefficient 12 den Gamma^2 - 12 (den - num) p_0^2 - SUM over the six Ports of R_ij is rule3's S: the general read and the derivations' Rule3 are one line where no tension stands.
rows.ground: exact rationals on four periodic boards

rows.name: Theorem 3, the conserved form
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The conserved form; the paper's Theorem 3; S.48
rows.statement: With D = diag(1 / p_i^2), p_i = p_0(i)^2 / Gamma, D M is symmetric under R_a(i -> j) = 2 num p_i^2 q_ij^2 / Gamma^2 with q_ij = q_ji, and Q(x, y) = x . D x + y . D y - x . D M y satisfies Q(a_next, a_now) = Q(a_now, a_before); E = w Q is exact for any field and any tensions before the integer remainders.
rows.ground: exact fractions on four periodic boards over several intervals, the vacuum's paces and the no-tension cases forced

rows.name: The plain form fails under a tension, S.32's two witnesses
rows.statement: Three Nodes at [1, 1], Gamma = 4, q = 2 (R = 8, w = 96, S = 144), now = (1, 0, 0): next = (11 / 6, 1 / 12, 1 / 12), the plain form from 6 to -21 / 4 and Eq. (6) 6; 3^3 Nodes at [2, 3], Gamma = 10, q = 5 (R = 100, w = 1,800, S = 1,800), a uniform 3 over 0: next = 4 with the remainder 0, the plain form per Node 162 to -54 and Eq. (6) 162 (4,374 over the board); at q = Gamma the two forms coincide.
rows.ground: exact fractions and integers

rows.name: The remainders' walk of the form
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The conserved form (the proof's last sentence), row 7 of The conventions and the units; the paper's 4.3
rows.statement: The integer step's next = next* + (r - r') / w adds to Q the walk SUM_i epsilon_i (next_i - before_i), epsilon_i = (r_i - r_i') / w, so E walks by SUM_i (r_i - r_i') (next_i - before_i) / p_i^2 (rule3.form_walk), each term below one unit of the level's change; E_3 walks by SUM_i [epsilon_i(t) next_i - epsilon_i(t + 1) now_i] / p_i^2.
rows.ground: exact integers on four boards with tensions, 40 intervals each

rows.name: The three-level form equals the two-level form
rows.place: row 7 of The conventions and the units; main.tex 4.3
rows.statement: Q = SUM_i (now_i^2 + before_i^2) / p_i^2 - (1 / w) SUM_i (SUM_j R_ij now_j + S_i now_i) before_i / p_i^2 equals E_3 = SUM_i (now_i^2 - next_i before_i) / p_i^2 exactly under the line, and D_i = b^2 sin^2 omega on a plane wave.
rows.ground: exact fractions on four boards with tensions and at rational angles

rows.name: The form's change under moving paces
rows.statement: Where the paces move, D = |a_now|^2 - <a_next, a_before> changes exactly by D(t + 1) - D(t) = <a_next, (M(t) - M(t + 1)^T) a_now>, and the weighted E with the weights of the paces at t + 1 by a_next^T D (M(t) - M(t + 1)) a_now.
rows.ground: exact fractions, two reads with different contents on three boards

rows.name: Theorem 1, the direction
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The direction; the paper's Theorem 1; S.48
rows.statement: The forward call (a_now, a_before, r) gives (a_next, r') and the backward call (a_now, a_next, r') gives (a_before, r) bit for bit; the proof's identities -floor(u / w) = ceil(-u / w) and ceil((w a - r) / w) = a for 0 <= r < w.
rows.ground: the identities over every residue at every wall to 40 (both sides shift by one with u + w); rule3.step and rule3.step_backward round trips at random integers

rows.name: The cube's symmetry: the complement identity
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The direction (The cube's symmetry), the proof's act (1)
rows.statement: floor((w - 1 - u) / w) = -floor(u / w) for every integer u, the ones' complement commuting with the floor division by a positive wall, its remainder w - 1 - r'; the zero-remainder lay's floor(-u / w) = -ceil(u / w) differs wherever w does not divide u.
rows.ground: every residue at every wall to 60

rows.name: The cube's symmetry act by act
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The direction (The cube's symmetry), the proof's acts (2) to (6)
rows.statement: A lay invariant under one of the cube's 48 with the complement remainders is invariant to the bit under every act of the step, so one fundamental domain steps the whole.
rows.ground: the engine's acts (the write, the reads, the time and Link turns); the integer identity of act (1) is row L23
rows.note: A statement of the engine's acts; tests/test_the_node.py and the symmetric lay's runs show it.

rows.name: The Wronskian with the form's weights
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The paces (The sign is the rotation sense); S.9
rows.statement: W = re_now^T D im_before - im_now^T D re_before is invariant under the line with D M symmetric; per Node W_i / p_i^2 changes by (2 num / w) (q_ij^2 / Gamma^2) (im_i re_j - re_i im_j) over the six Ports, (num / (3 den)) per Port for the integer W_i at the vacuum; S.9's chain of three at Gamma = 2 (W_0 from 0 to 3, the current 3 / 4) and the integer counterexample at [2, 3], (1, 3) over zeros to (1, 4), W from 0 to -1.
rows.ground: exact fractions on four boards with tensions; rule3.step for the witnesses

rows.name: The sign current's flux over density
rows.statement: For the plane record the density is w A^2 sin omega and the flux through a Link R_a A^2 sin k_a, so flux over density is (R_a / w) sin k_a / sin omega = d omega / dk_a, the current rho v exactly; J_a = g_(i, i+a) + g_(i-a, i) = 2 A^2 sin k_a = (6 den / num) W v at the vacuum's paces.
rows.ground: exact Gaussian rationals at rational angles

rows.name: The velocity invariant of the massless row
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md at 915c6a7b, The click writes on the lattice (the restoring front's third test; the front is history at 3a334eeb under the dense record's clause, the identity of the line standing); ENGINE.md, the face's kicks
rows.statement: For a record at uniform paces with S + SUM R = 2 w the velocity sum SUM now - SUM before is kept by the line and the integer V = w (SUM now - SUM before) + SUM r is exactly invariant on a periodic board; for a gapped pair it moves by -12 (den - num) Gamma^2 SUM now per interval.
rows.ground: exact integers by rule3.step on four periodic boards, 100 intervals

rows.name: The write's total is exact over any window
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The integer-exact constructions (4); The integer budget of a derived row
rows.statement: The sum over n intervals of the written q_t is (the sum of the numerators + r_0 - r_n) / w exactly, in (-1, 1) of the line's sum; the remainders' terms telescope to (r_0 - r_n) / w.
rows.ground: exact integers at random numerators and walls

rows.name: The booking identity of the hole
rows.place: S.50 (R289); ALGEBRA.md, The click is the meeting
rows.statement: Q(p, q) = SUM_i [w p_i^2 + w q_i^2 - p_i (S q_i + SUM_j R_ij q_j)] at uniform coefficients satisfies Q(next, now) = Q(now, before) and Q(now, before) = w SUM_i D_i; a face writing x for the level v the step would write changes Q by (x - v) [w (x + v) - (S now_i + SUM_j R_ij now_j)] = w (x - v) (x - b), at most w (v - b)^2 / 4 removed at the midpoint.
rows.ground: exact fractions on three periodic boards

rows.name: The share identity at any paces
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The share's change is the currents; the paper's Eq. (10); S.5
rows.statement: e_i(next*, now) - e_i(now, before) = SUM_j (q_ij^2 / Gamma^2) F_ij, since R_ij / (2 p_i^2) = num q_ij^2 / Gamma^2 is the same from both ends; the integer step adds -(next_i - before_i) (r'_i - r_i) / (2 p_i^2); S.5's witnesses, the chain of five at [2, 3] and the uniform 3 over 0 reading 81 where the mean-of-paces form read 324.

rows.name: The share is conserved at standing paces
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The count is the record's share (Theorem); main.tex 4.4
rows.statement: Over any region whose paces stand, SUM e_i changes in one step by the weighted currents through the region's boundary Links and the remainder terms alone, the interior Links cancelling by F_ji = -F_ij and q_ji = q_ij.
rows.ground: exact fractions on a chain of five with a region of two and the whole board

rows.name: The vacuum's share
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The count is the record's share; main.tex Eq. (9)
rows.statement: At the vacuum's paces the share is exactly 3 den (now_i^2 + before_i^2) - num now_i S_6(before)_i.

rows.name: The plane wave's current and form
rows.statement: A plane record travelling from i to j has F_ij = -2 num |psi|^2 sin omega sin k summed over its two lines; one real line has F = -num A^2 sin omega sin k exactly at every Node with no oscillating part, and D = A^2 sin^2 omega.
rows.ground: exact at rational angles

rows.name: The momentum flux identity with the remainders
rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The tension; the paper's Eq. (7); row 5 of The conventions and the units; S.48
rows.statement: At uniform coefficients w [P_a(t + 1) - P_a(t)] = SUM_b R_b [G_ab(i) - G_ab(i - b)] with G_ab(i) = now_i (now_(i+a+b) - now_(i-a+b)) - now_(i+b) (now_(i+a) - now_(i-a)); with the rounding the identity holds up to -[delta_i Delta_a now_i - now_i Delta_a delta_i], delta = r - r', exactly; and G_aa(i) = h_a(i) + h_a(i + a).

rows.statement: For now_i = b cos(k x_i + phi) along the axis G_aa = -2 b^2 sin^2 k at every Node, the Link's booking 2 num b^2 sin^2 k and the Node's tension T_aa = -num h_a = num b^2 sin^2 k; the cross reading G_ab = -2 b^2 sin k_a sin k_b.

rows.statement: The share's one-sided form and the hole's symmetric form agree summed over the board with the share's weight 1 / p_i^2 inside, SUM_i a_i SUM_j R_ij b_j / p_i^2 = SUM_i b_i SUM_j R_ij a_j / p_i^2, and differ at a Node; without the weight they agree at uniform paces.

rows.name: The exact lay's operator line
rows.statement: With L the line's own read, (L f)_i = (S f_i + SUM over the six Ports of R f_j) / (2 w), of eigenvalue cos omega(q) on e^(i q x), the record one interval earlier is z_(-1) = (L + i sqrt(1 - L^2)) z, so before = L a - sqrt(1 - L^2) s exactly with the backward root 0; the expansion about c = cos omega_k, before_i = (c a_i - s_k s_i) + [(L a)_i - c a_i] + (c / s_k) [(L s)_i - c s_i] + O((L - c)^2), its remainder (1 / 2) f'' (L - c)^2 with f = sqrt(1 - L^2), f'' = -1 / s_k^3 and L - c = -s_k v_g delta, -v_g^2 delta^2 / (2 s_k); the plain lay's backward root 0.02991 at delta = 0.05 and 0.05662 at 0.10 against the first order 0.03173 and 0.06345.

rows.statement: g_00 = -e^(-2 U) = -(1 - 2 U + 2 U^2) + O(U^3) and g_ij = e^(2 U) delta_ij = (1 + 2 U + 2 U^2) delta_ij + O(U^3): gamma = 1 exactly and beta = 1 in U; the remainders -4 U^3 / 3 and 4 U^3 / 3.

rows.place: S.18; the paper's Eq. (14); ALGEBRA.md, The method of derivation
rows.statement: m* = 3 den sin omega_0 / num = 3 tan omega_0; a = [num / (3 den sin omega_0)] [2 g / sin omega_0] |grad U| = 2 cos omega_0 / (3 (1 + cos omega_0)) |grad U| = [(1 - epsilon) / (3 (1 - epsilon / 2))] |grad U| in the gap epsilon, 4 / 15 at [2, 3] and 1 / 3 as the gap closes; U_K = [2 cos omega_0 / (1 + cos omega_0)] U, 4 / 5 at [2, 3] and 1 as the gap closes.

rows.name: The moving clock to the fourth order
rows.place: S.21; main.tex 8 (e); ALGEBRA.md, The rows against nature (e)
rows.statement: omega(k) = omega_0 + alpha k^2 - beta k^4 + O(k^6) with alpha = c_0 / (2 s) and beta = c_0 / (24 s) + c c_0^2 / (8 s^3); Omega / omega_0 = 1 - v^2 / (2 c_m^2) - (2 omega_0 / sin 2 omega_0) v^4 / (8 c_m^4) + O(v^6), c_m^2 = omega_0 / (3 tan omega_0): Lorentz's factor at c_m to the second order exactly, the fourth order's factor 2 omega_0 / sin 2 omega_0 = 1.6926 at [2, 3], along n omega_0 [(SUM n_a^4) tan omega_0 + cot omega_0], 1.2224 on a face diagonal, 1.0657 on the body diagonal, 1 as the gap closes; S.21's check -3.37 and -2.12 against -3.365 and -2.119.

rows.statement: With E^2 = m^2 + P^2, m = N omega_0, P = c N^2 k, -(d omega / dU)_k = (E^2 + P^2) / E = E (1 + beta^2); the exact line F_perp = grad U [2 (1 - nu) e^(-2 U) + (4 nu / 3) e^(-4 U) SUM_a (1 - cos k_a)] / sin omega; at [2, 3] the rest push over E is f(omega_0) = 1.0634 and the coefficient of beta^2 over it 1.3354 = gamma_K - alpha_K / 2; at [999, 1000] 1.00017 and 1.00067.

rows.statement: The four sums' squares add to M_1^2 + M_2^2 (Lagrange's identity); E(a, b) = cos 2a cos 2b + rho sin 2a sin 2b with rho = 2 M_1 M_2 / (M_1^2 + M_2^2); P(A+) = (M_1^2 c_a^2 + M_2^2 s_a^2) / (M_1^2 + M_2^2) independent of b; equal parts give cos 2(a - b); at (1, 0), (1, 1), (12, 5), (5, 12): 119 / 169, -119 / 169, 120 / 169, 120 / 169, S = 478 / 169 = 2.8284 below 2 sqrt 2, and S = (238 + 240 rho) / 169 at unequal parts.

rows.place: ALGEBRA.md, The integer-exact constructions (3), row 9; S.61 row 9
rows.statement: sin theta = 2 p q / (p^2 + q^2) and cos theta = (p^2 - q^2) / (p^2 + q^2) exactly on the circle; R(theta) = S_x S_y S_x with t = tan(theta / 2) and sin theta = 2 t / (1 + t^2), an identity of 2 x 2 matrices.

rows.name: The units of one quantum

rows.statement: (W_c sin omega_0)^2 = 9 T^2 (den^2 - num^2), the count wall; A^2 = count T den / (2 laid sqrt(den^2 - num^2)) gives 2 A^2 sin omega = (count / laid) T; one quantum's share 6 den A^2 sin^2 omega = W_c sin omega; the Wronskian |W| = A^2 sin omega = T / 2 for a charged circular quantum (0 for a real record, S.49 (4) since d7e97674), so one quantum writes 1 / (2 E_s) and |q_p| = |q_e|; |W| / (count T) = 1 / (2 sin omega_0) = 0.6708 for a record laid by share at [2, 3] and 1 / 2 for a record of count 1.

rows.statement: |SUM_(y = 0)^(n - 1) e^(2 pi i y / Lambda)| = sin(pi n / Lambda) / sin(pi / Lambda), the factor sin(pi n / Lambda) / (n sin(pi / Lambda)), 0.91 at n = 4, Lambda = 16, and 0 at Lambda = n.

rows.statement: F(R) = K / R^2 - SUM_r sigma_r W_r R^(-s_r): F'(1) = 0 is the virial 2 K = SUM sigma s W and F''(1) = SUM sigma s (2 - s) W under it; s (2 - s) = +1, 0, -3 at s = 1, 2, 3; Pekar's F = a / R^2 - c / R has one critical point 2 a / c, a minimum for every mass.

rows.statement: F = a / R^2 - b / R^3 - c / R has F' = (c R^2 - 2 a R + 3 b) / R^4, the roots R_+- = (a +- sqrt(a^2 - 3 b c)) / c, none where 3 b c > a^2; F'' = 2 (a R - 3 b) / R^5 at a root, the wide point the minimum and the narrow the saddle.

rows.name: The functional's gradient is the fixed point's equation
rows.place: S.13; ALGEBRA.md, The functional (Proof); the paper's Eq. (12)
rows.statement: dF / dphi_i = (2 num / (3 den)) (-Delta^2 phi)_i - (8 g / Gamma) Phi_i phi_i with Phi the wells of the record's own counts, so dF / dphi = -2 (M(Phi) phi - 2 cos omega_0 phi) and dF / dphi = 2 lambda phi on the sphere is the fixed point's equation with lambda = 2 cos omega_0 - 2 cos omega_b.

rows.name: The adiabatic invariant and the count's drift
rows.statement: At fixed omega D_t = a_t^2 - a_(t+1) a_(t-1) = a_t^2 + a_(t-1)^2 - 2 cos omega a_t a_(t-1) is conserved and equals A^2 sin^2 omega; the orbits are ellipses of area pi D / sin omega, so D / sin omega = A^2 sin omega is the adiabatic invariant, the slowly varying ansatz with the midpoint phase satisfying the line to the first order in the ramp; the recurrence stepped 20,000 intervals from 0.841 to 0.600 keeps D / sin omega within 4 x 10^-5 while D falls by a quarter; N(t_2) / N(t_1) = [sin omega_b(t_2) / sin omega_b(t_1)] [p_i^2(t_1) / p_i^2(t_2)].

rows.statement: sin omega_j - sin omega_i = 2 cos((omega_i + omega_j) / 2) sin((omega_j - omega_i) / 2) = sin(omega_j - omega_i) [1 - omega_i omega_j / 2 + O(omega^4)]: one photon's share T sin omega_L at the line, to a relative omega_0^2 / 2 at nature's gap.

rows.statement: Re[e^(-i omega_0 (t + 1)) (psi + psi' + psi'' / 2) + e^(-i omega_0 (t - 1)) (psi - psi' + psi'' / 2)] = Re[e^(-i omega_0 t) (2 cos omega_0 psi - 2 i sin omega_0 psi' + cos omega_0 psi'')] exactly; (num / (3 den)) 6 = 2 cos omega_0; i psi' = -Delta psi / (2 m*) with m* = 3 den sin omega_0 / num = 3 tan omega_0; the three conditions, the band's k^4 term of relative size k^2 / 12 and psi'' against 2 sin omega_0 psi' of relative size (omega - omega_0) / (2 tan omega_0).

rows.statement: zeta' = -i (Delta / 2) zeta - i mu e^(i theta) conj(zeta) has the exponents +- sqrt(mu^2 - Delta^2 / 4): growth for |Delta| < 2 mu, a full width epsilon / sin omega_b with mu = epsilon / (4 sin omega_b).
